added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(0<h<H\leq1\) such that \(H^{-1}\) and \(H/h\) are positive integers and every macro cube of side \(H\) contains at least two fine cubes of side \(h\).  Consider the nested macro--fine prior described below, with independent Rademacher macro signs \(\sigma_Q\), fine coefficients \(U_j=q_e\varepsilon_j\) and \(V_j=q_b\eta_j\), and \(0<\delta\leq q_eq_b\).  Under the alternative prior let
\[
 {\mathbb P}_1(\varepsilon_j=a,\eta_j=b)=\frac14,
\]
and, conditional on \(\sigma_Q\), under the constant-CATE null prior let
\[
 {\mathbb P}_0(\varepsilon_j=a,\eta_j=b\mid\sigma_Q)
 =\frac14\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\},\qquad
 \vartheta=\frac{\delta}{q_eq_b},\qquad a,b\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Then the coordinate means vanish, \(U_j^2=q_e^2\), \(V_j^2=q_b^2\), and
\[
 {\mathbb E}_0(U_jV_j\mid\sigma_Q)-{\mathbb E}_1(U_jV_j)
 =\delta\sigma_Q.
\]
With the interior reference \(e_\star=1/2\), \(m_{0,\star}=3/8\), and \(\tau_\star=1/8\), the induced null and alternative prior-predictive laws match for one observation conditional on all macro signs.  They also match for two observations lying in distinct fine cells, conditional on the macro signs.  However, take observations \(1,2\) in one fine cell and observation \(3\) in a distinct fine cell of the same macro cube.  If
\[
 \xi_i=s_e(A_i)B_i,\qquad \upsilon_i=s_b(A_i,Y_i)B_i,\qquad
 \kappa_i=\xi_i\upsilon_i,
\]
where
\[
 s_e(a)=2(2a-1),\qquad
 s_b(a,y)=\begin{cases}-8/5,&(a,y)=(0,0),\\ 8/3,&(a,y)=(0,1),\\ -2,&(a,y)=(1,0),\\ 2,&(a,y)=(1,1),\end{cases}
\]
and \(B_i\) is the active fine bump at \(X_i\), then the exact third canonical projection of the null-minus-alternative prior-predictive likelihood ratio is
\[
 \delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3,\qquad
 \mathcal L_{12}
 =(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)
 -(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2)(\kappa_1+\kappa_2).
\]
This projection is not identically zero.  For fixed nonzero collar bumps, its contribution to the squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) norm is bounded below by
\[
 c_b(n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4
\]
for a constant \(c_b>0\) depending only on the bump and \(d\).  At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h=\delta^5\), \(H=\delta\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\), this term has order \(n^{1/3}\), whereas the charged same-fine term \(n^2h\delta^4\) has order \(n^{-2/5}\) and the proposed four-observation term \(n^4h^2H\delta^4\) has order one.  Consequently the requested support-controlled expansion for this exact four-atom prior cannot omit the cross-fine third-order term.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(r=\delta\sigma_Q\).  The four displayed masses defining \({\mathbb P}_0\) are nonnegative because \(0\leq\vartheta\leq1\), and their sum is one because
\[
 \sum_{a,b\in\{-1,1\}}ab=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 {\mathbb E}_0(\varepsilon_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}a\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}=0,\\
 {\mathbb E}_0(\eta_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}b\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}=0,\\
 {\mathbb E}_0(\varepsilon_j\eta_j\mid\sigma_Q)
 &=\frac14\sum_{a,b}ab\{1+\vartheta\sigma_Qab\}
 =\vartheta\sigma_Q.
 \end{aligned}                                                    \tag{1}
\]
The corresponding expectations under \({\mathbb P}_1\) are zero.  Since \(\varepsilon_j^2=\eta_j^2=1\), multiplying (1) by \(q_e\), \(q_b\), or \(q_eq_b\), as appropriate, proves all asserted coordinate moment identities.

For completeness, these coefficient laws are compatible with the original binary class whenever the ordinary deterministic bump restrictions are imposed.  Namely, let
\[
 u=\sum_jU_jB_j,\qquad v=\sum_jV_jB_j,\qquad
 G=\sum_Q\sigma_QG_Q,\qquad G_Q=\sum_{j\subset Q}B_j^2,
\]
and define every null component by
\[
 e_0=\frac12+u,\qquad m_{0,0}=\frac38+v,\qquad \tau_0\equiv\frac18,   \tag{2}
\]
and every alternative component by
\[
 e_1=\frac12+u,\qquad
 m_{0,1}=\frac38+v-2\delta G,\qquad
 \tau_1=\frac18+4\delta G.                                          \tag{3}
\]
Suppose the collar construction has, for a constant \(C_b\) depending only on its fixed shape and on \(d\),
\[
 \left[\sum_j a_jB_j\right]_s\leq C_bh^{-s}\max_j|a_j|,\qquad
 \left[\sum_Q z_QG_Q\right]_s\leq C_bH^{-s}\max_Q|z_Q|,              \tag{4}
\]
for \(s\in\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}\), as well as the corresponding sup-norm bounds with right side \(\max_j|a_j|\) and \(\max_Q|z_Q|\).  The conditions
\[
 C_bq_eh^{-\alpha}\leq L,\qquad
 C_b\{q_bh^{-\beta}+2\delta H^{-\beta}\}\leq L,\qquad
 4C_b\delta H^{-\gamma}\leq L                                      \tag{5}
\]
then give, respectively, the propensity, baseline, and CATE Hölder restrictions by (2)--(4).  If
\[
 q_e\leq\frac14,\qquad q_b+2\delta\leq\frac18,                       \tag{6}
\]
then (2)--(3) imply pointwise
\[
 \frac14\leq e_k\leq\frac34,\qquad
 \frac14\leq m_{0,k}\leq\frac34,\qquad
 \frac14\leq m_{0,k}+\tau_k\leq\frac34,\qquad k\in\{0,1\}.           \tag{7}
\]
The null effect in (2) is exactly constant.  Taking \(X\) uniform, drawing \(A\mid X\) as Bernoulli with mean \(e_k(X)\), drawing binary \(Y(0),Y(1)\) conditionally independently of \(A\) given \(X\) with means \(m_{0,k}(X)\) and \(m_{0,k}(X)+\tau_k(X)\), and setting \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\), verifies exact uniform design, conditional exchangeability, consistency, and binary support.  Thus (4)--(6) verify membership in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\); they are construction-side inequalities, not extra model assumptions.

It remains to compute the predictive likelihood.  Relative to the reference conditional probabilities
\[
 (p^\star_{00},p^\star_{01},p^\star_{10},p^\star_{11})
 =\left(\frac5{16},\frac3{16},\frac14,\frac14\right),                \tag{8}
\]
direct multiplication of the four Bernoulli cells in (2) gives, on a region where fine bump \(B_j\) is active,
\[
 L_{0,i}=(1+\xi_iU_j)(1+\upsilon_iV_j).                              \tag{9}
\]
For (3), the control-regression perturbation is \(V_jB_j-2rB_j^2\) and the treated-regression perturbation is \(V_jB_j+2rB_j^2\).  Dividing the resulting four cells by (8) therefore gives exactly
\[
 L_{1,i}=(1+\xi_iU_j)(1+\upsilon_iV_j+\kappa_ir).                    \tag{10}
\]
No remainder is used in (9)--(10).

Taking expectations in (9), using (1), gives
\[
 {\mathbb E}_0(L_{0,i}\mid\sigma_Q)=1+\kappa_ir.
\]
Under \({\mathbb P}_1\), \(U_j\) and \(V_j\) are independent and centered, so (10) gives the same expression:
\[
 {\mathbb E}_1(L_{1,i}\mid\sigma_Q)=1+\kappa_ir.                     \tag{11}
\]
This proves conditional one-observation matching.  If two observations use distinct fine coordinates, independence of their coefficient pairs makes both predictive likelihoods the product of the two common factors in (11).  This proves exact cancellation of the two-singleton cross-fine term claimed in the directive.

Now let observations \(1,2\) use the same fine coordinate.  Fixed squares and the vanishing odd mixed moments from (1) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 N_{12}:={\mathbb E}_0(L_{0,1}L_{0,2}\mid\sigma_Q)
 ={}&1+\xi_1\xi_2q_e^2+\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_b^2
 +(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)r\\
 &+\xi_1\xi_2\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_e^2q_b^2,                         \tag{12}\\
 A_{12}:={\mathbb E}_1(L_{1,1}L_{1,2}\mid\sigma_Q)
 ={}&(1+\xi_1\xi_2q_e^2)
 \{(1+\kappa_1r)(1+\kappa_2r)+\upsilon_1\upsilon_2q_b^2\}.           \tag{13}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting (13) from (12) gives
\[
 N_{12}-A_{12}=r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12},\qquad
 \mathcal Q_{12}=\kappa_1\kappa_2(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2),                \tag{14}
\]
with \(\mathcal L_{12}\) as in the statement.  Because observation \(3\) uses a distinct fine coordinate, its common conditional predictive factor is \(1+\kappa_3r\) by (11).  Hence the three-observation null-minus-alternative marginal is
\[
 (r\mathcal L_{12}-r^2\mathcal Q_{12})(1+\kappa_3r).                 \tag{15}
\]
Averaging (14)--(15) over the symmetric sign, for which \({\mathbb E}r=0\), \({\mathbb E}r^2=\delta^2\), and \({\mathbb E}r^3=0\), gives
\[
 F_{12}=-\delta^2\mathcal Q_{12},\qquad
 F_{123}=\delta^2(\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3-\mathcal Q_{12}).          \tag{16}
\]
The other two pairwise differences vanish because those pairs use distinct fine coordinates.  Since the one-observation differences vanish by (11), subtracting all lower-coordinate marginals from \(F_{123}\) shows that its third canonical projection is exactly
\[
 F_{123}-F_{12}-F_{13}-F_{23}=\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3.       \tag{17}
\]

This function is nonzero.  For example, if the three binary rows are all \((A_i,Y_i)=(1,1)\), then \(\xi_i=\upsilon_i=2B_i\), \(\kappa_i=4B_i^2\), and
\[
 \mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3
 =32B_1B_2B_3^2\{1-2q_e^2(B_1^2+B_2^2)\}.                            \tag{18}
\]
For \(q_e\leq1/4\) and \(0\leq B_i\leq1\), the factor in braces is at least \(3/4\); it is strictly positive whenever the three bump values are positive.

We finally make the cluster size explicit.  Under (8), \({\mathbb E}_\star\kappa_3=0\).  Indeed,
\[
 \sum_{a,y}p^\star_{ay}s_e(a)s_b(a,y)=1-1-1+1=0.                    \tag{19}
\]
Thus (17) is orthogonal to the same-fine second projection in (16), not merely pointwise different from it.  Equation (18), on an event of reference probability \(4^{-3}\), supplies a fixed positive lower bound on the conditional squared norm of (17) proportional to
\[
 \delta^4B_1^2B_2^2B_3^4.                                          \tag{20}
\]
Let \(c_2=\int B_{\mathrm{base}}^2>0\) and \(c_4=\int B_{\mathrm{base}}^4>0\).  Integration over one ordered pair of distinct fine cells in one macro cube turns (20) into a fixed multiple of \(\delta^4h^{3d}\).  There are
\[
 H^{-d}\left(\frac Hh\right)^d\left\{\left(\frac Hh\right)^d-1\right\}
 \asymp H^dh^{-2d}                                                   \tag{21}
\]
such ordered pairs.  Equations (20)--(21) therefore give a lower bound \(c_b\delta^4h^dH^d\) for the squared norm of the third canonical kernel.  Canonical kernels attached to distinct triples of sample coordinates are orthogonal: in the product of two such kernels there is a coordinate appearing in only one triple, and integration in that coordinate is zero by canonicality.  Summing over triples consequently gives
\[
 \left\|\overline L_{0,n}-\overline L_{1,n}\right\|_{L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})}^2
 \geq c_b\binom n3h^dH^d\delta^4,                                   \tag{22}
\]
up to absorbing the fixed factor \(6\) into \(c_b\).  This proves the asserted \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\) contribution.

At the required stress point, \(h=\delta^5\), \(H=\delta\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\).  Direct substitution gives
\[
 n^2h\delta^4=n^2\delta^9=n^{-2/5},\qquad
 n^4h^2H\delta^4=n^4\delta^{15}=1,                                  \tag{23}
\]
but
\[
 n^3hH\delta^4=n^3\delta^{10}=n^{1/3}.                              \tag{24}
\]
The coefficient laws themselves therefore pass the moment, margin, support, and two-singleton checks, and the same-fine residual is indeed subdominant, but the exact cross-fine \(2+1\) canonical projection (17) survives and is not dominated at the proposed rate.  This is the claimed obstruction for this prior and completes the proof.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a different bounded constant-null-supported nested prior whose exact fixed-sample likelihood cancels the nonzero cross-fine third canonical projection in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection}\), or derive an alternative comparison that controls it at the desired scale; then prove the matching sparse-occupancy upper theorem and optimize the independent lower and upper maps in every regime.
open_obligations.obstruction: For the prescribed four-atom law, conditional one-observation matching and independence do cancel two observations in distinct fine cells, and the same-fine residual is subdominant at the stress scale.  But a same-fine pair multiplied by the common singleton factor in a distinct fine cell leaves the exact third canonical coefficient \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\).  Its squared likelihood contribution is at least of order \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\), which equals \(n^{1/3}\) at \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h=\delta^5\), \(H=\delta\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\).  Thus the required support-controlled lower envelope does not close for this exact law, so no independent optimization match or definition of \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) is justified.
open_obligations.attempted: The calculation verified the four atomic probabilities, all first and second coordinate moments, the construction-side margin and Hölder inequalities, exact one-observation matching, and exact two-singleton cross-fine cancellation.  It then expanded the shared-fine two-observation factors without a remainder, multiplied by the distinct-fine singleton factor, averaged the macro sign, subtracted all lower-coordinate marginals, and computed the resulting third canonical projection and its spatial \(L^2\) scale.  The mandated stress substitution shows this term diverges while the same-fine term vanishes and the proposed fourth-order term stays bounded.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The already established unchanged-class bracket remains
\[
 c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n,\qquad
 b_n=\begin{cases}
 n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\leq4t,\\
 n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t,
 \end{cases}\qquad t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\},                    \tag{1}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), then
\[
 \rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},          \tag{2}
\]
and \(d=4\gamma\) carries no logarithm in this proved subregion.

For the newly prescribed bounded four-atom law, all coordinate means vanish, the squares are fixed, and
\[
 {\mathbb E}_0(U_jV_j\mid\sigma_Q)-{\mathbb E}_1(U_jV_j)
 =\delta\sigma_Q.
\]
The original binary margins and all three Hölder conditions follow from the explicit amplitude inequalities in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection}\).  Conditional one-observation matching is exact, and independence across distinct fine-coordinate pairs cancels the two-singleton cross-fine term exactly.  Nevertheless, for observations \(1,2\) in one fine cell and observation \(3\) in a distinct fine cell in the same macro cube, the third canonical likelihood projection equals
\[
 \delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3,\qquad
 \mathcal L_{12}
 =(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)
 -(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2)(\kappa_1+\kappa_2),                            \tag{3}
\]
and is not identically zero.  Its squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) contribution is at least a fixed multiple of
\[
 (n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4.                                                \tag{4}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h=\delta^5\), \(H=\delta\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\), the same-fine term is \(n^{-2/5}\), the proposed fourth-order term is one, but (4) is \(n^{1/3}\).  Thus the exact four-atom lower construction does not deliver the proposed candidate frontier.  A different bounded prior that cancels (3), or an alternative fixed-sample comparison controlling it at the desired scale, is required before the matching upper statistic and all-regime optimization can settle the target.  The two frozen optimizations remain diagnostics, and \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) remains undefined.

prose_updates.tldr: The proved result remains an honest all-regime bracket for the fixed-sample observational critical radius, together with the known-propensity benchmark and a matched no-penalty subregion.  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), the radius lies between \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\) and the explicit single-scale rate \(n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), or \(n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  If \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), both sides equal the known-propensity order \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\).  The prescribed four-atom nested prior satisfies the moment, margin, Hölder, one-observation, and two-singleton checks, and its same-fine residual is subdominant at the proposed rough scale.  An exact \(2+1\) fine-cell calculation nevertheless leaves a nonzero third canonical likelihood projection of squared scale \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\); it diverges at the mandated rough stress point.  Hence the complete frontier remains open and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Existing homogeneity tests provide asymptotic validity, fixed-direction power, or finite-stratum comparisons, while existing minimax work concerns different testing geometries or pointwise CATE estimation.  On the identical binary uniform-design causal class, the unresolved object is a matching fixed-sample lower and upper detection map across all three Hölder indices and all occupancy regimes.  The current exact likelihood audit shows that matching one observation and cross-fine singleton pairs is insufficient: mixed fine-cell occupancy can create a lower-order canonical term.
project_justification.niche: The live mathematical niche is the likelihood-level interaction among an unknown constant-effect null, separate propensity and baseline roughness, macro-scale CATE variation, and fine-scale repeated-observation collisions.  A sharp result must preserve exact uniform design, keep every null-prior component homogeneous, and control the full connected macro--fine expansion, including mixed occupancies such as a repeated fine cell plus a distinct singleton.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution supplies an explicit total single-scale fourth-order test, an all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark, and a matched no-penalty subregion.  The new exact calculation verifies the proposed four-atom coefficient law and its two-singleton cancellation, then identifies the surviving third canonical projection \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\) and its scale \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\).  This is a precise kill test for that lower construction, not a solution of the all-regime frontier.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen mixture envelope is invalid as a universal converse handle because a legal positive-CATE tuple is hidden in its nominal high-order remainder, and the frozen testing envelope is not sharp because it turns an unconditional first-projection floor into a fourth-root distance loss.  For the nested repair, the prescribed four-atom law has valid masses, zero coordinate means, fixed squares, and the required null-versus-alternative correlation difference.  It yields exact conditional one-observation matching, and independence across distinct fine coordinates exactly cancels the two-singleton cross-fine term.  The charged same-fine residual is subdominant at \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\).  However, a shared-fine pair and a distinct-fine singleton in the same macro cube have third canonical likelihood projection \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\), whose squared contribution is of order \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\) and therefore equals \(n^{1/3}\) at that stress point.  A different prior or an additional exact cancellation is required before a support-controlled converse, the matching upper collision theorem, or the all-regime optimization can be claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal estimand remains the centered \(L^2\) norm of the CATE, and the statistical class remains the original binary uniform-design Hölder class with fixed overlap and interior margins.  The known-propensity rate is a comparator and carries no novelty claim.  The proved observational content is the all-regime bracket and the sufficient no-penalty region; smoothness adaptation is not claimed.  The exact four-atom calculation is a construction-specific negative diagnostic: it disproves the proposed truncated cluster envelope but does not prove that every null-supported prior must incur the same third-order term.  The old deterministic mixture and testing optimizations remain regression tests, not definitions of the minimax radius.  The complete rough-nuisance frontier, equality-case logarithms outside the proved region, and the necessary-and-sufficient propensity-value frontier remain open.  No conclusion certifies a fitted forest, and non-rejection is not evidence that the CATE is constant.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the field-tier theorem target: it requires a total uniformly calibrated test and an original fixed-\(n\), constant-null-supported converse on the identical class, followed by an independent optimization match.
statement_notes.gap: The prescribed four-atom law satisfies the requested marginal moments, class-side inequalities, one-observation matching, and cross-fine singleton-pair cancellation.  The first surviving mixed-occupancy term is now explicit: a same-fine pair plus a distinct-fine singleton has third canonical projection \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\), contributing \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\) on the squared likelihood scale.  It diverges at the proposed rough stress rate, so this lower construction does not support the desired converse.  A replacement cancellation or comparison, the matching upper concentration theorem, and the all-regime optimization are still missing.
statement_notes.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying any fitted forest or converting non-rejection into a homogeneity conclusion.
